newsitem.title: MEXICO: Prison riot in Mexico City leaves 37 injured.
newsitem.headline: Prison riot in Mexico City leaves 37 injured.

text.p: Thirty-seven prisoners were injured on Thursday when about 200 police and guards broke up a riot in a prison in Mexico City, the government's National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) said.
"The CNDH could verify that during the operation referred to, 37 prisoners were injured with wounds of different degrees, who required emergency medical attention," a statement said.
It said inmates in the high-security wing of the male Reclusorio Varonil Oriental prison took two guards hostage during the riot, which began on Wednesday.
During the ordeal, two guards were also injured, though it was not clear if they were the two seized by the rioters.
The CNDH said it was investigating the police action but did not suggest there had been any wrongdoing.

Mexico City prisons have been in the spotlight recently after evidence emerged that wealthy inmates such as druglords live in luxury in at least one jail, enjoying imported foods and a gymnasium. The revelations forced the resignation of the head of the Mexico City prison system last week.
